title: Sheinbaum: If They Don’t Want to Participate in the 2027 Elections, Let Them Stay Out
author: Denisse Torres Hernández
content:
_This article by[Denisse Torres
Hernández](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/denissetorres/) originally
appeared in the [November 26, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4910321/pan-y-pri-dicen-que-abandonaran-
eleccion-de-2027-si-se-mantiene-sobrerrepresentacion/), a Mexican digital news
outlet._

_Opposition legislators questioned the impartiality of the electoral
authorities ahead of the upcoming decision on the rules for allocating seats
in the Chamber of Deputies._

**Mexico City, November 26 (SinEmbargo).-** The [**opposition** in
**Mexico**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/ultraderecha-en-mexico/) threatened
to withdraw from the **2027** **midterm** **elections** if the **National
Electoral Institute (INE)** maintains the criteria for allocating
**proportional-representation** **seats** that allowed **Morena** and its
allies to secure a supermajority in the **Chamber** **of** **Deputies**.
**President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo** responded that, if the parties decide
not to compete, that will be their own decision, but rejected the claim that
there is **overrepresentation**.

At her [morning press conference](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/la-mananera-
del-pueblo/), the president defended the interpretation of [electoral
legislation](https://www.ine.mx/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Despen-LEGIPE-
NormaINE.pdf) used to distribute **proportional** **representation** **seats**
, and maintained that the same provisions were applied in the 2015, 2018, 2021
and 2024 elections.

> “If they don’t want to participate, then let them stay out. It’s a political
> party’s decision. It’s their decision.”
>
> Claudia Sheinbaum, President of Mexico

She said this when asked about the opposition parties’ warning.

She also insisted that there was no formula to favor the ruling parties, but
rather the application of the legal provisions establishing how seats must be
allocated. She even recalled that the PAN, the PRI, Movimiento Ciudadano (MC)
and the now-defunct Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) approved that
legislation.

> “First, there is no overrepresentation formula, and I have already shown
> that. The Federal Law on Electoral Procedures was applied, which everyone
> can read, and they can see perfectly well how, point by point, it says
> exactly what must be done for proportional representation,” she maintained.

She also considered that the opposition parties’ dissatisfaction stems from
having won fewer seats than they expected in the last election, and even made
an ironic remark about the possibility that one of them might prefer not to
stand in the elections because it does not know how many votes it will get.

> “Maybe this political party has trouble knowing how many people are going to
> vote for it, and so it prefers not to stand, because it doesn’t make sense…
> I mean, how does a political party whose objective is to participate in an
> election decide not to participate in an election? Well, it’s their
> decision,” she added.

Although she defended the application of the current rules, Sheinbaum
acknowledged that the final decision rests with the electoral authorities.
“That is my point of view; obviously, the INE and the Tribunal have the final
say,” she noted.

President Sheinbaum Pardo’s response came after the coordinator of PAN
senators, Ricardo Anaya, warned yesterday that his party was not ruling out
any measure, including the possibility of refraining from competing for the
500 seats in San Lázaro.

![Claudia Sheinbaum addresses reporters at a press
conference.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/sheinbaum-opposition-2027-elections-body-1.jpg)Claudia
Sheinbaum recalled that the electoral legislation was also approved by the
opposition parties. Photo: Presidency.

“Everything is on the table,” said the legislator, who demanded that the INE’s
General Council not repeat the interpretation applied in 2024 to distribute
proportional-representation seats.

> “The National Action Party’s Parliamentary Group in the Senate of the
> Republic forcefully demands that the General Council of the National
> Electoral Institute, at its session next Monday, not dare to carry out the
> theft, the robbery, the fraud that overrepresentation represents,” he
> stated.

Anaya maintained that keeping that criterion would mean that the electoral
body had ceased to be an impartial and trustworthy referee. “We are not going
to accept the theft,” he declared, warning that the PAN would not recognize a
distribution that, from his perspective, favors the governing party.

> “If the INE once again gives Morena a path to overrepresentation, that is,
> to end up with far more deputies than citizens give them at the ballot box,
> it will be clear that there is no impartial and trustworthy electoral
> referee for the 2027 election. Masks off!” he said.

“It is time for the National Electoral Institute to state very clearly next
Monday whether they are an impartial referee, whether they are on the side of
democracy, or whether they are Morena’s stooges and are going to allow
overrepresentation once again,” he added.

![Opposition legislators hold signs opposing overrepresentation at a press
event.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/sheinbaum-
opposition-2027-elections-body-2.jpg)Ricardo Anaya warned that the PAN could
refrain from participating in the 2027 elections. Photo: Galo Cañas,
Cuartoscuro.

He also stressed that “this is very easy to understand: in no democracy in the
world is it acceptable for a coalition, as was the case with the current
ruling coalition led by Morena, to have 54 percent of the votes, practically
half, and end up with 73 percent of the deputies in the Chamber of Deputies.”

## PAN and PRI Question Rules for Allocating Seats

The position was echoed by the PRI, whose secretary-general, Carolina
Viggiano, said the party is also considering various protest actions against
the electoral body’s ruling, from occupying its offices to refraining from
participating in the 2027 electoral contest.

For his part, the PRI’s national leader, Alejandro Moreno, announced that the
party will challenge the agreement the INE is preparing on overrepresentation.
He also asked the Attorney General’s Office (FGR) to investigate the alleged
irregularities attributed to the electoral body’s former president, Guadalupe
Taddei, and to people linked to the awarding of contracts.

> “We are going to challenge it. It shouldn’t be,” he announced, emphasizing
> the importance of the INE, ahead of the 2027 elections, “behaving
> impartially, clearly and firmly, as what it is, the electoral referee,
> rather than having an electoral body that is on its knees, that is an
> employee of Morena’s cynical and corrupt government.”

> [Post by @RicardoAnayaC on
> X](https://x.com/RicardoAnayaC/status/2125739280475832392)

Moreno maintained that the PRI has already filed a complaint with the Attorney
General’s Office and alleged that there is a corruption network within the
Institute. He also called on the electoral authorities to act independently of
the federal government.
